## Hello!

My name is **Joseph Bailey**. I'm a Data Scientist currently managing a team of Data Scientists
and Engineers at the BBC. I work at the intersection of [AI]{.mark-lime}, data and people. I love
exploring data, data visualisation, programming and helping others to get joy from the same things.
My favourite languages are R and Python.

Much of my programming interest is geared toward geospatial visualisation and spatial algorithms.
I also have a passion for learning more about leadership in technical roles and generative art.

This blog is where I think out loud: experiments with models, analysis in Python and R, maps,
creative coding, and lessons from leading teams. Newer posts are Quarto notebooks, so the code you
see is the code that made the charts.

Outside of this domain, I also like adventure racing and triathlons.

## What you'll find here

- **AI**: models, evaluations and what actually works in production.
- **Data**: analysis, visualisation, geospatial work and conference notes.
- **Art**: generative pieces, ray-traced maps and creative coding.
- **Leadership**: notes on teams, decisions and growing people.
- **Other**: everything that doesn't fit neatly.

## Background

I have worked at:

- BBC (current)
- Connected Places Catapult, formerly Future Cities Catapult
- Simon Fraser University
- Geotrace
- Apple

## Projects

- [**Geogrid**](https://github.com/jbaileyh/geogrid): turn geospatial polygons like states, counties or local authorities into regular or hexagonal grids automatically.

## Papers & presentations

I have presented at a range of professional and academic conferences, mostly on the use of data
in environmental science, urban science and transport modelling.
